component: Third-party components compiled into the bundled Windows FFmpeg tool pair

applies_to.binaries_note: ffprobe.exe was removed from the desktop payload by app PR #101, but every public release through 0.8.0+993 shipped it and the source-availability obligation runs to those recipients. It is named here deliberately and must not be tidied out. Both executables share one provider, revision and configure line, so the component list is identical for both.
applies_to.linkage: static; the two executables are self-contained
applies_to.invocation: the app runs the tools as subprocesses and does not link FFmpeg libraries

derivation.method: parsed the `configuration:` line captured from the exact shipped binary
authority_for_licence_classes: repo-extracted FFmpeg LICENSE.md (source tarball ffmpeg-n8.1.1-13-g83e8541aa6-source.tar.gz), filed at repo:docs/release/evidence/license-sources/ffmpeg/LICENSE-FFmpeg.md
repo-extracted FFmpeg configure: EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_GPL_LIST / _NONFREE_LIST / _VERSION3_LIST / _GPLV3_LIST, filed at repo:docs/release/evidence/ffmpeg-components/ffmpeg-configure-license-lists.md
per-component upstream licence files and repository metadata
derivation.exclusion_rationale: --enable-version3 is a licence-election switch; --enable-pthreads selects a threading model; --enable-cuda-llvm selects how CUDA kernels are compiled; --enable-schannel uses the Windows TLS API rather than a redistributed library. None is a third-party component shipped inside the binaries.
derivation.prior_count_reconciliation: The prior count of 58 is confirmed and reproduces exactly as 62 --enable- flags minus the four non-component switches above. It is nevertheless an undercount of what is actually inside the binaries: see toolchain_components, which the configure line does not name.
derivation.linkage_field_semantics: `linkage_confirmed` is present only on entries where linkage could NOT be confirmed by symbol or string probe, and is always false there. Its absence means linkage was either confirmed (see the entry's notes) or not separately probed. Added 2026-08-08 so the unconfirmed set is machine-locatable rather than inferable only from open_gaps prose.

scope_boundary.statement: This derivation is EXACT for the configure line and BLIND ONE LEVEL DOWN, by construction rather than by oversight. A library that arrives as a dependency of an enabled component has no --enable- flag, so there is nothing here to parse and nothing in configure's EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_GPL_LIST to match - that list is keyed on FFmpeg's own flag names.
scope_boundary.demonstrated_by: FFTW (GPL-2.0-or-later) is statically compiled into this binary via chromaprint's FFT backend, and libudfread (LGPL-2.1-or-later) via libbluray. Neither is nameable from the configure line.
scope_boundary.effect_on_summary_below: None of the counts in `summary` change. All twelve newly found transitive components are attribution-only, and the two that carry a source obligation (fftw3, libudfread) were already known. The counts remain correct for their own scope; they are simply not a statement about the whole binary, and `gpl_only_components: 0` in particular must never be quoted as 'no GPL code in the binary'.

summary.needs_review_count_correction: This field read 4 from 2026-08-07 until 2026-08-08. Only three entries carry a NEEDS-REVIEW marker and no fourth could be reconciled to any entry, so the count is corrected to 3 and the members are now named. Do not restore 4 without naming the fourth. The likely source of the confusion is the separate set of FOUR components whose linkage could not be confirmed by probe - a different axis, now carried as `linkage_confirmed: false` and counted in `linkage_unconfirmed` below.
summary.gpl_only_components_semantics: Counts configure-line components FFmpeg itself classifies as GPL-only. It is NOT a statement that no GPL code is in the binary, and must never be restated as one. GPL code IS present by two paths this field cannot see: FFTW (GPL-2.0-or-later), a transitive dependency of chromaprint; and part of libzvbi (GPL-2.0-only in src/packet-830.* and src/pdc.*), invisible to a whole-component SPDX id because the tree is per-file mixed. Corrected 2026-08-09 by S&C.
gpl_code_present_paths: libzvbi src/packet-830.* - GPL-2.0-only, treated as present on the unconditional source-level call chain (undeterminable by binary measurement); src/pdc.* same licence, positive evidence of ABSENCE measured 2026-08-09 (app PR #139; method and limits in docs/release/evidence/ffmpeg/libzvbi-gpl2-linkage-measurement.md). Until 2026-08-09 this entry read 'link-reachable' for packet-830.* and 'linkage not established' for pdc.*. The measurement narrows the exposure and withdraws nothing - libzvbi stays disclosed and its source stays published.
summary.needs_review_correction_2026_08_09: libzvbi left this list on 2026-08-09 because reading its source resolved the question - AGAINST the earlier classification, not in its favour. It is now recorded as partly GPL-2.0-only. Removing it from needs-review is not a clearance.

gpl_and_nonfree_check.result: CLEAN AS TO THE CONFIGURE LINE
gpl_and_nonfree_check.method: Cross-checked every enabled flag against FFmpeg configure's own EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_GPL_LIST, EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_NONFREE_LIST and EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_GPLV3_LIST, extracted from the matching source revision.
gpl_and_nonfree_check.note: --enable-version3 is not optional decoration: four enabled components require it. Removing it would make the build non-distributable, so LGPL-3.0-or-later is the correct and necessary licence for the tool pair.
gpl_and_nonfree_check.result_scope_correction_2026_08_09: Previously reported as an unqualified 'CLEAN'. That phrasing has now been the proximate cause of two wrong public statements - the FFTW miss and the in-app notice claiming no GPL-only component is present. The check is correct and correctly run; it is authoritative for direct configure-line components as FFmpeg classifies them, and blind by construction to (1) transitive dependencies and (2) per-file mixed licensing inside a component. Both blind spots have produced real GPL code in the shipped binary. A CLEAN here means 'no enabled component is on FFmpeg's GPL-only list' and nothing more.
gpl_and_nonfree_check.gpl_list_members_enabled_note: Empty on FFmpeg's own list. See result_scope_correction_2026_08_09.

ijg_credit.requirement: FFmpeg LICENSE.md: libavcodec/jfdctfst.c, libavcodec/jfdctint_template.c and libavcodec/jrevdct.c are taken from libjpeg. Because we distribute executables only, we must credit the Independent JPEG Group in the accompanying documentation, and must indicate any changes (additions and deletions) to those three files.
ijg_credit.our_position: No Inter Galactic modifications were made; the binaries are unmodified upstream BtbN builds.

freetype_credit.requirement: The FreeType Licence (FTL) requires a specific credit line in the documentation when the FTL is elected over the GPL-2.0 alternative.
freetype_credit.status: MUST APPEAR IN THE NOTICE; the dual-licence election must be recorded

open_gaps: Upstream component VERSIONS are not recorded anywhere we hold. The FFmpeg configure line names components but not versions, and BtbN pins them in its own build scripts. Two classifications (libkvazaar, libzmq) are version-dependent, and a defensible SBOM needs the pinned versions regardless.

CLOSED 2026-08-09 - corresponding source for every obligated component (the 16 here plus the transitive fftw3 and libudfread) is published at https://app.ourgalaxy.space/source/, each cut at its exact pinned commit; commits and digests are in docs/release/evidence/corresponding-source-holding/HOLDING.json. This gap read 'No corresponding source is currently mirrored for any of the 16 components carrying a source obligation. Only the FFmpeg source tarball itself is held.'
Static linkage means LGPL-2.1 sec.6 / LGPL-3 sec.4 relink provisions are engaged for each LGPL-family component, not merely source availability.

Linkage could not be confirmed by symbol probe for chromaprint, libharfbuzz, libsnappy and libuavs3d. Only chromaprint materially matters (it is LGPL-family) and it is counted as present, which is the conservative direction. These four now carry `linkage_confirmed: false` so they can be found from the data rather than from this sentence.

libzvbi is per-file mixed and part of it is GPL-2.0-only (src/packet-830.*, src/pdc.*). A whole-component SPDX id cannot express that, and the inventory schema currently has one id per component. Any future component added here needs a per-file check, not just an upstream id lookup - the same class of miss as FFTW, on a different axis. Corrected entries carry a license_breakdown object; the schema should make that the norm.

UPDATED 2026-08-09 (app PR #139) - both linkage statuses moved, in opposite directions. pdc.o now has positive evidence of ABSENCE: three format strings in pdc.c that compile unconditionally (each verified to sit outside any preprocessor conditional) are all missing from the shipped ffmpeg.exe, while 'libzvbi' appears 12 times in the same binary as a working control. Evidence rather than proof - --gc-sections/LTO can strip an unreferenced function with its constants. packet-830.o is downgraded from established to UNDETERMINABLE BY MEASUREMENT (no surviving string literals, no surviving symbol names, no map file or unstripped build) and is treated as present on the source-level call chain, the conservative reading. Method: docs/release/evidence/ffmpeg/libzvbi-gpl2-linkage-measurement.md. This gap read 'Whether pdc.o is linked into the shipped ffmpeg.exe is NOT established and cannot be settled from source alone. It needs the build's map file or an unstripped build. packet-830.o IS established as link-reachable.' The measurement narrows the exposure and withdraws nothing.

components.corrected: 2026-08-09 by S&C. Previously recorded LGPL-2.1-only on the strength of VideoLAN's project description. That is contradicted by the component's own source at the pinned commit and the earlier value was wrong.
components.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-09. Verified against the held archive libbluray-g4dfb9b0123b0-source.tar.gz at commit 4dfb9b0123b006ce5d66592dc8058f61e5c0cdc8. 845 files carry 'version 2.1 of the License, or (at your option) any later version'; ZERO files in the tree state 2.1 without 'or later'. Two non-LGPL sets exist and neither is in the linked library: jni/*.h are MPL-1.1/GPL-2.0+/LGPL-2.1+ tri-licensed (LGPL-2.1-or-later electable), and src/devtools/bdj_test.c is GPL-2.0-or-later but is a devtool absent from the library build. Consequence: libbluray CAN elect v3 and therefore does have access to GPL-3 section 8 cure, contrary to the earlier record.

components.name: libzvbi
components.license_id_note: A single SPDX id cannot express this component. The tree is mixed and the GPL-2.0-only part is not severable from the linked library.
components.obligation_class: attribution + source availability (GPL-family, escalated from LGPL-family)
components.classification_basis: source and COPYING.md at the pinned commit, plus the upstream build definition
components.corrected: 2026-08-09 by S&C. Previously LGPL-2.0-or-later at medium confidence, needs-review, resting on distribution metadata. Reading the source settles it: the single-id classification was incomplete, not merely unconfirmed.
components.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-09. Verified against the held archive libzvbi-g41477c97c8ed-source.tar.gz at commit 41477c97c8edf7a01f1594b2a95b94f0117eed21. COPYING.md is per-directory and states verbatim: 'The files src/packet-830.* and src/pdc.* have the following copyright and license: License: GPL-2'. The four files themselves carry 'under the terms of the GNU General Public License version 2 as published by the Free Software Foundation' with NO 'or later'. Four files, not two - the .h files carry the same header as the .c files. ESTABLISHED that packet-830 reaches the executable: src/Makefile.am puts packet-830.c/.h and pdc.c/.h in libzvbi_la_SOURCES, and there is an unconditional link-time chain from FFmpeg - libavcodec/libzvbi-teletextdec.c:679 calls vbi_decode -> src/vbi.c:472 vbi_decode_teletext -> src/packet.c:2686 parse_8_30 -> src/packet.c:2146/2165 call vbi_decode_teletext_8301_local_time and vbi_decode_teletext_8302_pdc, both defined in packet-830.c. The event_mask tests at those call sites are runtime guards, not link-time ones, so a static link must pull packet-830.o. NOT ESTABLISHED for pdc.o: no cross-translation-unit reference to any pdc.c-defined symbol exists, so on a standard static link it would not be pulled - but that is an inference about linker behaviour, not a fact about this binary, and settling it needs the build map file or an unstripped build. Consequence: the GPL-2.0-only files have no 'or later', so no v3 election and no GPL-3 section 8 cure is available for them. CORRECTED AGAIN LATER THE SAME DAY (REVIEW, app PR #139): both linkage statuses above have moved. pdc.o now has positive evidence of ABSENCE - three pdc.c format strings that compile unconditionally are all missing from the shipped ffmpeg.exe, with 'libzvbi' x12 in the same binary as the working control; still evidence rather than proof under --gc-sections/LTO. packet-830.o is UNDETERMINABLE BY MEASUREMENT rather than established - nothing of it survives compilation to search for (no literals, and symbol names do not survive the strip either; even vbi_decode appears zero times) - so its presence rests on the source-level chain described above and it is treated as present, the conservative reading. The licence-consequence sentence is unchanged. Method, controls and reproduction: docs/release/evidence/ffmpeg/libzvbi-gpl2-linkage-measurement.md.
components.prior_probe_retracted: A string probe of the shipped ffmpeg.exe searched for the literals 'Europe/London' and 'Indefinite time window' and found neither, which was read as evidence the objects were not linked. That probe was incapable of a positive result and is retracted as evidence in either direction: both literals occur ONLY inside C comments in pdc.c (lines 804, 994, 1382 and 1237, 1452), and the preprocessor strips comments before compilation, so they could never appear in any binary whether or not the file was linked.

toolchain_components.name: libgomp
toolchain_components.notes: Pulled in by --extra-libs=-lgomp, not by any --enable- flag, so it is invisible to a configure-line-only inventory. VERIFIED LINKED: 'GOMP_target_enter_exit_data' plus 36 distinct omp_* symbols in ffmpeg.exe. This is GPL-3 code inside an LGPL-3 binary; the GCC Runtime Library Exception is what makes that lawful, and it holds here because the build used GCC 15.2.0 (an Eligible Compilation Process). Worth stating explicitly so a later audit does not read it as GPL contamination.
